slides.title: Main sessions (New York time)
head: Session
Hours (ET)
slides.text: Approximate, standard time. Shifts by an hour when daylight saving changes.

points.t: 9:30–11:00 ET: the most volume and the biggest moves for US index futures.
Both centers open: liquidity peaks for currencies.
15:00–16:00 ET: volume picks up again into the end of the day.
Lunch hours: thinner volume, more chop.
Moves happen, but with a fraction of the day's volume.

points.b: Trade when your market is active

points.t: 8:30 and 10:00 ET data releases move markets in seconds.
Many traders find one window does most of their damage.

slides.title: Same market, different hours, different behaviour.
slides.text: Pick the window that fits your strategy, and log which hours actually work for you.

post.instagram:
Futures trade almost 24 hours, but volume doesn't. For US index futures the New York open (9:30–11:00 ET) is the busiest window, midday is often slow and choppy, and volume picks up again into the close. Check 8:30 and 10:00 ET data releases, and track your own results by hour.

Save this for later and follow @calmedgeofficial for one trading concept a day.

Educational content. Not financial advice; trading involves risk of loss.
